newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iran's Rafsanjani arrives in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Rafsanjani arrives in Turkey.

text.p: Iranian President Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani arrived in Turkey on Thursday for a visit aimed at building on growing trade links despite U.S. efforts to isolate Iran.
"I believe the subjects we will talk about here will benefit our countries and people," Rafsanjani told reporters at Ankara airport.

Speaking after a full military inspection, Turkish president Suleyman Demirel said: "I believe that we will achieve important results during Mr Rafsanjani's visit in terms of developing economic and trade relations."

A senior Turkish official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters details of a preliminary study for building a pipeline to carry Iranian oil to Western markets through Turkey's Mediterranean terminal of Ceyhan would be discussed during the visit.
Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan, visited Iran in August and signed a $23 billion agreement for the supply of Iranian natural gas over 23 years.
The deal was struck days after U.S. President Bill Clinton signed a law imposing sanctions on any country investing more than $40 million a year in the energy industries of Iran or Libya.
Turkish and Iranian economy officials have been meeting in Ankara this week on new agreements on trade, shipping and the foundation of a joint chamber of commerce.

Rafsanjani, who arrived with a large delegation, was quoted by the Iranian news agency IRNA as saying his talks would cover the latest developments in the Gulf and Kurdish-controlled northern Iraq. His visit will last four days.

Relations between the two countries have been strained by concerns in Ankara that Kurdish separatists, seeking self-rule in the southeast of Turkey, have used Iran as a springboard for attacks in the east.
Demirel said talks would include matters of order, security and "the struggle against terrorism".
Iran, like much of the Moslem world, was angered earlier this year when Turkey signed a deal with Israel, allowing Israeli air force planes to train in Turkish airspace.
